cohort: 70 patients who underwent amniocentesis for any reason were included, divided into an adverse pregnancy outcome group (n=35) and controls (n=35).
finding: Lower levels of amniotic fluid tenascin X (<20.7ng/ml) and serum tenascin X (≤1.97ng/ml) were significantly associated with and predicted adverse perinatal outcomes, including gestational diabetes, preterm birth, premature rupture of membranes, and low Apgar score.
